title: WHERE Clause & Filtering Logic
description: Filter datasets with comparison operators, pattern matching, case-insensitive ILIKE, and understand how the planner utilizes index scans.

data.text: The **`WHERE`** clause specifies search conditions (predicates) that filter rows before aggregation or projection. Rows are included in the result set only if the search condition evaluates to `TRUE`.

rows: Case-sensitive pattern matching (`%` matches any sequence, `_` matches single char)
Three-valued logic check for missing/unknown data

data.text: A query is **SARGable** (Search Argument Able) when the database query optimizer can leverage an index to locate rows. Wrapping indexed columns in functions disables B-tree index usage unless an expression index exists!

data.title: Non-SARGable vs SARGable Filtering
data.content: Notice how modifying the column side invalidates standard indexes.
data.code:
-- ❌ NON-SARGABLE: Wraps created_at in DATE() function; forces full table scan!
SELECT id FROM users 
WHERE DATE(created_at) = '2024-01-15';

-- ✅ SARGABLE: Leaves column untouched; uses B-tree index on created_at
SELECT id FROM users 
WHERE created_at >= '2024-01-15 00:00:00' 
  AND created_at <  '2024-01-16 00:00:00';

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: `WHERE` filters rows based on predicates evaluating to boolean `TRUE`.
Use `ILIKE` for case-insensitive matching without manual `LOWER()` calls.
Keep columns free of function wrappers to maintain index seek capability (SARGability).
